subject: Request for SLA credit — calculation dispute over maintenance window & partial degradation
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeanalytics.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA credit request — calculation during maintenance + CDN degradation

Hi Priyom,

We're reviewing the invoice and SLA report for June and believe the uptime calculation is incorrect. On June 18 between 02:05–03:20 UTC our service experienced elevated tail latency and partial request failures; our monitoring shows ~18 minutes of severe degradation and another ~35 minutes of elevated p95. Redwood's team labeled this as a "third-party CDN event" and excluded it, but Acme's agreement explicitly references service availability to end-users regardless of upstream dependencies. Additionally, the monthly 1-hour scheduled maintenance window was applied as a 60-minute exclusion — we had planned maintenance overlapping that timestamp window and we don't think that should nullify the period where customers saw degraded experience outside the scheduled maintenance start/end.

We're requesting a credit calculation aligned with the contract's definition of "downtime affecting end-user transactions" and a detailed breakdown of how Redwood arrived at the 99.98% uptime reported. I've attached our consolidated incident timeline and a short calculation sheet we used. Please let me know who at Redwood will confirm the adjusted credit and timeline — procurement would like a resolution this week to close the invoice.

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Analytics

Attachment: SLA_calculation_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA credit request — calculation during maintenance + CDN degradation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear write-up and the spreadsheet. I opened SUP-4382 so our ops team can reconcile timelines. Quick notes:

- We do respect the contract wording; however, there are clear clauses that exclude scheduled maintenance windows and incidents attributable to third-party providers (with a defined notification process).
- That said, I understand your view about user-facing impact when maintenance windows overlap. I’ve looped in Monica (CS) and Marcus (Legal/Contracts) to review the specific timestamps and the wording you cited.

Monica — can you pick this up for the credit calculation? Marcus — would appreciate a read on the contract carve-outs and whether an exception/goodwill credit is appropriate. Sarah — we may need the raw request logs for the affected endpoints if you can share them; that will speed validation.

I’ll follow up by EOD Monday with next steps.

—Priyom

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, sarah.jenkins@acmeanalytics.com
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA credit request — calculation during maintenance + CDN degradation

Hi all — I pulled the incident timeline from our side and attached the vendor report for the CDN (cdn_incident_report.pdf). Summary of findings:

1) June 18 02:00–03:30 UTC — Origin observed increased error rates starting at ~02:05 UTC; the third-party CDN reported a regional configuration failure at 02:07 UTC and declared mitigation at 02:45 UTC. However, we recorded residual elevated latency until ~03:20 UTC due to cache priming and downstream queueing.
2) Our scheduled maintenance window for June was 02:00–03:00 UTC on the 18th; the maintenance started as planned at 02:00 and concluded at 02:55 UTC. The maintenance was for a non-customer-facing config change but did coincide technically with the CDN incident start.
3) Per contract: scheduled maintenance windows up to 60 minutes are excluded from uptime calculations if customers were notified and change was non-user impacting.

Given the overlap, the pure "downtime" directly attributable to our service (post-CDN mitigation) is ~18 minutes (02:57–03:15 UTC) where requests failed at the origin. The customer's monitoring shows elevated p95 earlier — that aligns with CDN-origin degradation and cache warming.

Proposed next steps:
- We validate request logs for Acme's top 3 endpoints (Sarah, if you upload the request logs we can map them)
- If agreed, Redwood will propose a blended credit: contract-entitled credit points for 18 minutes of Redwood-attributable downtime plus a one-time goodwill credit (to acknowledge degraded experience during overlap) equal to 25% of the calculated contract credit.

Marcus — any legal constraints on issuing a goodwill credit absent an explicit breach?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: cdn_incident_report.pdf (PDF stub)

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, sarah.jenkins@acmeanalytics.com
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA credit request — calculation during maintenance + CDN degradation

Quick legal note: contract sections 6.1–6.3 define exclusions clearly. There is room to provide a goodwill concession (non-precedential) so long as we document it as a one-time credit and avoid wording that implies acceptance of wider liability. Recommend the following language in the customer-facing note: 

"Redwood has investigated the June 18 event. Our findings indicate 18 minutes of downtime attributable to Redwood systems outside of scheduled maintenance and CDN mitigation. In recognition of the customer experience during the overlapping maintenance and third-party outage, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 25% of the calculated contractual credit. This goodwill credit is not an admission of breach and does not change the terms of the SLA."

If Acme agrees to that language, we can issue a statement and the credit. Also recommend we attach the vendor report and our timeline as an annex for transparency.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA credit request — calculation during maintenance + CDN degradation

Hi Sarah — thanks for your patience and for the logs you uploaded (confirmed receipt). We reviewed both timelines and agree on the following resolution: 

1) Redwood confirms 18 minutes of downtime attributable to Redwood systems outside the scheduled maintenance window.
2) In addition to the contractual credit, Redwood will issue a one-time goodwill credit equal to 25% of the contractual credit calculation.
3) We'll send the formal credit statement and a single-line invoice adjustment by end of day tomorrow. This credit is issued as a non-precedential goodwill gesture and does not alter the SLA terms.

If that sounds acceptable, please reply with approval and I'll route the credit. Appreciate the collaborative approach here.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
